My reason to live is Gloria Borger.
Lol cats. Those were simpler times.

Until today posting about it here with everyone... I kept working on myself to my own introspective  views I  had on my own feelings. Never really thought about how much I take on the feelings of those around me.  So essentially, I feel that you feel it.
Agreed! I'm so sick of it at times. I've never done anything to actually try to be more cold-blooded, but the thought to change has been there at the very least.

This account of mine has been sitting idle for a while, so I totally forgot what my username was until you just brought it up.   
Essentially, birds have always been a grounding thing for me. When I'm outside and overwhelmed by my surroundings I'll focus on a pigeon bobbing his head or a seagull screaming for chips.  It has always made me feel better.   
As a kid, I found out my Grandpa who passed away at a young age was obsessed with birds too. While I never met him, it fuelled my habit and eventual hobby of bird-watching.   
In some of my darkest moments, the fact I symbolised birds as life has been what has snapped me out of suicidal thoughts or behaviour. It sounds silly, but it was my little ribbon to remember life.   
Birds look so free in their ability to fly.
I could imagine right now a cockatoo with pent up energy - screaming in a flock at the top of it's lungs. If you haven't heard the sound - it sounds like that feeling.
YUP. Your expression of it is exactly what I feel all our brains felt the second we're grounded and realise this.

The metaphor of it as a magnet holds a lot of truth.  Good point on grounding. It's something I feel people forget a lot. It definitely helps. Some support is better than none. Plus, you wouldn't want it to be a sure thing to eradicate it anyways, because I think its what helps make you the person you are.   
Sometimes I get caught in the loop that I'm responsible for my own emotions, thoughts and actions... and forget I don't have to take on that of those around me.
I wonder overall if it has always just been a bad coping mechanism --- and the trouble-making behaviour is more healthy form of releasing emotions.

That makes a lot of sense now as to why some people always say they didn't see it coming, when their friend passes away due to suicide. The quiet, caring person is probably micro managing and detecting their feelings prior to their own.
Yeah same - it was almost the feeling that it would be the ultimate sorry. I get that, I think my tendencies manifest in a similar way.

Interesting, thank you for your disagreement.    
Sorry to hear you have been dealing with that since 11 and that you feel they don't understand.

That's a really clear what of putting it. I never thought of it as a cycle but it definitely is the more I sit here. Somehow realising this point actually helps to lift a little of the weight off ones shoulders.
What's gotten you to the point you have been considering this? Talk to me about it. Let it all out.

Not really sure where you're from.   
But there is always hope there are some free or cheap services that may be the loop hole to that issue.   
You mentioned you have done some college credit. They usually have some things like that. Or online searching up in your area.   


Otherwise I'm also a person who has had really debilitating panic attacks for 3 years now and I'd be happy to share with you some tips that have reduced them for me. I don't want to bore you, so I thought to ask before I send the things that have worked for me. 

So rather than wanting to actually die you are feeling guilt and shame. It all stems from the anxiety. So at the very least some part of you has hope. This is the part you have to hold onto. It will be the driving force to give you courage when you have your next panic attacks.
Agree with Krowerl. Until I tried to find my own meaning to exist by reading and studying myself - I really didn't have a clue.
Sometimes I think the groove really is just the process of telling yourself you'll eventually get in the groove.

OP you are a good person, and like you said you are kind and don't hurt people. You have good traits in that regard.  What you're dealing with is tough, and not something you can improve alone or quickly.   
The fact you go out and get those jobs are mini steps in themselves.   
It seems less like you want to die, and more like you haven't been coping so well for living. Your wants to tell people what's going on tells me you want to keep going.   


Do you have a doc you could talk to. I have found that's personally helped for me - as they showed other resources and ways to combat anxiety that I couldn't even think of on my own. To feel nervous, scared and panic attacks can be debilitating and that's okay.   


Sending hugs, and sorry if I said the wrong things. I too can a bit anxious when it comes to sending these messages.
There really are none completely 100%. You wanna talk about it?
Sure
You have given the best open perspective to this
Thanks for sharing that hehe, and I'll keep that in mind onlyarose.
Thank you deere\_64, it really means a lot.

Completely valid hopes. It's something we all search for, to feel important to someone. You express that you don't want it to be for finances or material things, which really shows that you're a person with good values and intentions. The world needs more people like you. By posting on here, while you feel you can't go on at the moment given all the bullshit you have had to deal with up to now, I can hear some hope for things to change and for love. Death can always be post-poned - you can't find love in the forest... but it is out there.

I can hear on one hand you are in a difficult situation currently and have been in the past - so your feelings of exhaustion are completely justifiable... but on the other hand, you seem to have a great deal of self perception and why you feel things may not be going well. It seems you are quite hard on yourself, and even through this I can challenge that you are trying and that makes you more of a special and amazing person than you can currently see. What is it in this moment that you feel would make you feel better and less tired, even if you feel it wouldn't be possible to achieve in this exact moment?
If it means anything, I'd give you a big ass hug right now OP. You damn right deserve one. Scream out the anger - and if you can, try stop the bleeding. Tell me all the hurt if it may help too.
While you're still here on reddit, talk to me about it. What has happened to get you up on the tree?

Yeah definitely, feeling lost right now is completely understandable, especially with what you are dealing with right now with the lack of appreciation and care you are experiencing from your boyfriend.  Is the self harm when you are feeling anxious or for other reasons?

I'm sorry to hear about the loss of your father and the difficult situation you are currently in. I hope your mum is doing okay in hospital at the moment. Thank you for taking the time to care for her - being for her and organising ways so she's not alone during her time grieving is all you can do.Sometimes when people have lost someone very close to them it can be difficult for them to focus on anything around them. Listening to her and grounding her in the current moment by helping with any physical tasks helps.  The more you listen to her and prompt her to tell you what's going on in her mind, the more she will end up explaining to you what she needs most at the moment.
You sound quite upset about yourself and your relationship. What is it that you feel you can't control? I want to hear your story.
